description: What upstream published, when it was last looked at, and whether a lag behind it was decided. This file records observations about external projects. It is not the pin registry, does not select a target, and authorizes no update. `external-pins.json` remains the sole owner of which artifact each qualification targets.

method.why_separate_from_the_registry: The registry records a decision; this file records a fact about someone else's project. Keeping them apart preserves `observed != adopted`: refreshing an observation must never look like moving a pin.
method.version_comparison: No mechanical comparison is made between `latest_seen` and the pinned version. Upstream identifiers are heterogeneous — Hermes Agent 0.20.6 ships as tag `v2026.8.27` — so a human records the `delta` verdict. The tool only detects that upstream moved past `latest_seen`.

delta_states.none: the pin is on the upstream head recorded here
delta_states.acknowledged: a newer upstream release exists and a dated human decision explains why the pin stays; this cannot close freshness for pins whose tracking_policy is follow_latest_stable
delta_states.open: a newer upstream release exists and no decision has been recorded

Deployed is not reviewed.

hindsight.note: The pin was moved to the observed head on 2026-08-31; the O1/O2/Q5 labs re-run against it on this change and their result is the qualification. It does not settle which lexical lane is authoritative on which corpus: 0.9.2's BM25 change overlaps the hand-written lexical fallback added to implementation/mvp_vertical/retrieval.py in Pantheon-Next#874, and Hindsight is not wired into that retrieval path, so the two lanes remain a separate open design question.

contrastive-lm.note: Contrastive-LM/CLM has no GitHub Release feed at this observation point, so the current default-branch commit was reviewed directly and pinned separately for the bounded Pantheon-Next#1047 shadow-ranking experiment. Package metadata at that ref reports contrastive-lm 0.1.0. Upstream issue #3 reports unexpected score behavior and PR #6 discusses long-state truncation semantics; this qualification therefore uses /v1/rank on short synthetic states only. Observation does not install, activate, route, authorize, admit Evidence, or adopt CLM. Quantized-encoder qualification additionally records the official Qwen/Qwen3-8B-GGUF Q8_0 and Q4_K_M artifacts by exact SHA-256 and llama.cpp v0.5.0 at commit 7fe450e19305b828c199d602c23a8337aaa1f03b. These are experimental encoder variants only; the pinned Qwen3-8B/vLLM path remains the numerical reference and no quantized variant is activated by registry presence.
